title: skyBlip device configuration (v1)
description: JSON config exchanged over the dedicated GATT characteristic / USB-CDC. The producer (firmware) owns this schema; consumers pin a version. Every key here is read by the firmware: settings with no reader were removed rather than accepted and ignored (region, rotation, power_save, dropped after v1.0; page_mask, dropped when the pad's walk became three pages nothing may hide; stealth and gyro, dropped with the features themselves). Every key is accepted on 'set'; every key but the two per-unit bench trims (battery_offset_mv, freq_trim_e1_ppm) is also returned by 'get', which is one BLE frame at the 182-byte payload the narrowest phone in the field carries and has nine bytes of headroom left at its worst case.

addr.description: 24-bit device address, read-only: the low 24 bits of the SoC unique id, taken the way an OGN tracker takes it, so one board is one aircraft whichever of the two firmwares it ran. It is not a stored setting, it is read from the silicon, so there is nothing to edit and a 'set' carrying this key is ignored like any key with no reader. The two values no decoder can read (0x000000 'no address', 0xFFFFFF a dead read) are answered with a fixed address

addr_table.description: ADS-L address mapping table (issue 2 F.2.2): 0=random/privacy, 1-4 reserved, 5=ICAO, 6=FLARM, 7=OGN-Tracker, 8=FANET, 9+ manufacturer pages, each a registry-assigned 8-bit prefix and a 16-bit base address. A constant 58 on this device, the entry applied for at registry@ads-l.aero with the prefix structuring waived so all 24 bits carry the address, read-only like addr: the address is the chip's, and a table claiming it came from anywhere else is the inconsistent configuration F.2.3 asks a device to disallow

units.description: 0=nautical (NM, kt), 1=metric (km, km/h): the aeronautical unit is the first one because it is the one a pilot flies, and a device ships on it. Decides every page that prints a distance or a speed: the radar's range ring, the nearby page's distance column, the six-pack's speed dial. Altitudes and vertical speeds stay in feet whatever this says, and the status page shows the aeronautical figure and the SI one side by side

battery_offset_mv.description: Per-unit battery gauge trim in millivolts, added to every reading before a state of charge or a cutoff is read into it. Set once on the production line against a bench supply: two 1% divider resistors put the ratio out by up to 2% (84 mV at a full cell) and the SAADC's gain and reference error adds to that, on a curve whose flat middle spends 250 mV crossing 60 percentage points. The bound is three times the divider's own worst case; beyond it the unit is wired wrong, not out of trim. Write-only over the link: the 'get' reply cannot carry another key (see the top-level description), and the trimmed reading is read back as the millivolts the status reply and the panel already show

freq_trim_e1_ppm.description: Radio centre-frequency trim in tenths of a ppm, positive upwards, applied to every dwell the SX1262 arms (receive and transmit alike). The board fits a TCXO, so 0 is the design intent and the expected value on every unit; the field exists because nothing on the device can measure the reference, and a batch of TCXOs ten times worse than its datasheet would otherwise be a recall. The bound is that tenfold miss (+-10 ppm, +-8.7 kHz at 868.2 MHz): inside it the carrier cannot leave ERC 70-03 band h1.4 (868.0-868.6 MHz), beyond it the part is broken rather than out of trim. Set only against a spectrum analyser or a frequency counter. Write-only over the link, like battery_offset_mv: the 'get' reply cannot carry another key (see the top-level description), and the device has nothing that could measure the value back for itself

callsign.description: Upper-case letters, digits, dash and blank, the characters the radar menu types and the ones a $PFLAA ID field can carry, and the aircraft's registration as the radio says it. Set on the radar menu or over this link, shown on the status page, reported back here, and transmitted once every ten seconds: ADS-L's own Traffic payload carries no name, so it goes out under payload type 66, the entry F.2.1 assigns to OGN and whose definition it leaves to them (TelemType 1, InfoType 5, 14 characters). Empty means nothing is transmitted, which is the default and the privacy answer: an address a receiver cannot resolve stays anonymous, and a registration in clear does not. Nine characters here against the wire's fourteen, because that is what the stored settings blob has always held
